text:
The error sat in the ledger like a stone in a shoe—small, unnoticed by the world, but grinding against Elara’s conscience. Julian argued for silence. "It’s trivial," he said, tapping his pen against the mahogany desk, his voice smooth as polished glass. "No one checks column B. To report it is to invite scrutiny we do not need. We protect our reputation by maintaining the illusion of perfection."

Elara looked at the numbers. They were just ink, yet they held weight. She thought of the client who would sign off, trusting the integrity she had sworn to uphold. If they hid this, the truth became a variable, subject to change whenever convenient. It was not about the sum; it was about the architecture of trust. A lie left uncorrected becomes a foundation. And foundations, when built on sand, eventually collapse under their own quiet weight.

She picked up her phone. The screen lit up, reflecting her steady gaze. Julian sighed, shaking his head at what he deemed foolishness. But Elara knew that precision was not merely about accuracy; it was about respect. She dialed. The click of the connection sounded less like a mistake being made, and more like a promise kept.
